Then even for the fiscal 2027 outlook, I know you said SG&A down year-over-year. You have sort of an unusual compare in fourth quarter. Can you give us a little bit of help on where you think the gross margin lands for fiscal 2027? Thank you.
investorQuestions.intent: 投资人希望补齐第二季度收入和毛利率节奏，以识别同比基数、折扣和供应链节省的净影响。
investorQuestions.replyFramework: 管理层不提供单点毛利率指引，改用供应链改善、折扣压力和同比高基数搭建方向性桥梁。
investorQuestions.exampleAnswer: Yeah, thank you. This is Dave. Actually, we are probably not going to provide guidance specifically for gross margin, but for the year. At this point in time, there are puts and takes. I think one thing that is really constructive from a gross margin perspective is we are making fairly significant moves in our supply chain and sourcing programs today. That is actually bolstering gross margin. At the same time, we are taking discounts and resetting the marketplace, which is dampening gross margins over time. So there is a little push and pull for this year as we go through the balance of fiscal 2027. I will say, as it relates to Q2, I just wanted to highlight, because of the actions that occurred last year, we are up against a tough comparison with what happened in Cyber Week in Europe as well as what happened in North America sell then last year, Q2. If you look sequentially quarter-over-quarter, you will see because of that comparison, growth rates being pressured in Q2. I hope that helps.
investorQuestions.tags: ["puts and takes","gross margin","tough comparison"]

investorQuestions.question: Great, thanks. So Elliott, could you elaborate on the level of potential pain before gain? It seems like that's a key theme here that you're laying out today. What segments of the business may further moderate type of the strategic actions that you noted would impact the business for the balance of this year and into early fiscal 2028? And just on Pace, would it be fiscal 2029 where we could expect this transformation work to bear fruit at a P&L level?
investorQuestions.intent: 投资人聚焦先承压后改善的持续时间，并追问 Pace 节省何时在损益表充分体现。
investorQuestions.replyFramework: 答复明确 Sportswear、Jordan 和中国的压力将延续至 FY2028，并给出 2029-2030 年节省规模化的时间锚。
investorQuestions.exampleAnswer: So maybe this is Dave, maybe I'll start. First, I think as we indicated, those three areas, whether it be Sportswear, Jordan Brand, and China, we're taking deliberate actions in those areas to improve performance for the long term, and that's going to dampen performance now. Yes, we're going to experience some, as you describe it, some additional pain. But I think that's going to be through the balance of this year and probably bleed in a little bit into fiscal 2028 as well. But that's all in the goal of returning these businesses to health and driving really outside shareholder value creation over time, number one. Secondly, as it relates to Pace, we are beginning to see savings now even through Q1. Some of the actions that we took as it related to supply chain are bearing fruit in gross margin. You're beginning to see some improvement in our P&L today from Pace. But clearly, the savings are going to ramp over time, starting now, with the maximum savings to be appreciated and accrued in 2029 and 2030.
investorQuestions.tags: ["pain before gain","P&L level","savings ramp"]

investorQuestions.question: Hey, guys. Thanks for taking our question. Let me add my welcome, Dave. It's nice to work with you.
investorQuestions.intent: 投资人同时检验中国恢复路径、公司收入转正时点和股息可持续性。
investorQuestions.replyFramework: 管理层先明确股息优先级，再把五年收入与利润框架留到投资者日披露。
investorQuestions.exampleAnswer: Nice. Yeah. First and foremost, let me hit that right out the gate. Dividend is a very significant priority for us here at Nike. It is a significant priority from the capital allocation program, and under all scenarios, we have support for maintaining and ultimately growing the dividend over time. Just we can put that to bed with that statement. Secondly, I look forward to spending some time with you in November, because in November, we're going to give you a financial algorithm so you can begin to assess what not just 2027 looks like, but what does the next five years begin to look like, both from a top-line and a bottom-line perspective. So, why don't we hold that question? We'll come back to it at Investor Day, and we'll hit that head on.
investorQuestions.tags: ["dividend priority","financial algorithm","top-line and bottom-line"]
